transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Nguyen (Redwood SE), Arjun Rao (Redwood Product), Sophie Chen (Atlas Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Atlas Platform), Rita Gomez (Atlas CTO)

Auto-generated summary: walkthrough of Optimize features; focus on batching and KV cache; agreed next steps to run benchmarks and share cost model.

00:00 Maya: hey everyone, thanks for making time, i know we're all tight on schedules. this is Maya from Redwood, i'll kick us off -- quick agenda: demo of Optimize, dive into batching heuristics and prefix / kv cache, then cost model mapping to your throughput. carlos will be doing the deep parts.
00:18 Sophie: thanks, maya. quick ask up front -- we care about latency at the 95th pct, and also our unit cost. so if we can see the tradeoff that'd be great.
00:25 Carlos: yep, totally. we'll show empirical numbers and then map to dollars per k tokens. also show what happens when cache hit-rate changes.
00:34 Maya: quick introductions -- sophie?
00:38 Sophie: sophie chen, head of ml at atlas, i manage ML infra and models.
00:41 Rita: rita gomez, cto -- i'm here for architecture and compliance questions.
00:44 Liam: liam o'connor, platform eng -- i'll share traffic profiles after the call.
00:50 Carlos: great. ok i'll share screen -- this is Redwood Optimize console. first block is batch sizing suggestions. so the heuristics look at your sequence length distribution, slack in latency SLO, and model throughput to recommend batch windows.
01:12 Carlos: empirical example -- for a 2k seq average and a 100ms token generation target, we recommend an adaptive batch window of 8-12ms which yields an effective batch size ~10 on our p4d-like shapes. that moves cost down ~22% in our tests but adds ~8-12ms to tail latency.
01:33 Sophie: can you explain the adaptation? like how do you avoid adding latency for single-request spikes?
01:40 Carlos: yeah so adaptive windows are traffic-aware -- if you get a single low-traffic request it'll flush earlier, there's a max-wait cap equal to 50% of your tail SLO. also we do early flush when requests wait beyond a flavour -- basically conservative defaults.
02:02 Arjun: and we couple that with prefix caching -- the console shows prefix/KV cache hit-rate and estimated token reuse. for Atlas's use-case (financial doc summarization) we saw common prefixes across user sessions so the cache is helpful.
02:18 Liam: quick Q -- is the KV cache per-customer or shared? we need strong tenant isolation.
02:23 Carlos: per-customer by default on Dedicated and Private; on Hosted we provide per-tenant logical namespaces with encryption and RBAC. encryption-at-rest via KMS and option to bring-your-own-key for private.
02:38 Rita: that helps. what about cache size and eviction policy? financial docs can be long.
02:44 Carlos: eviction is LRU with TTLs configurable; we recommend tiered TTLs by prompt family -- short-lived for interactive prompts, longer for templated docs. we showed a chart where increasing cache from 10k to 50k entries moved hit-rate from 18% to 46% for a doc-heavy workload.
03:05 Sophie: showed earlier that cost model -- can you walk through the dollars?
03:09 Carlos: sure. here's the simplified model: baseline cost per token at small batch = C0. effective per-token compute cost drops roughly with sqrt(batch) until you saturate kernel efficiency; then batching gives diminishing returns. caching reduces generated tokens because prefix tokens are read from KV not regenerated -- effective tokens billed drop by hit_rate * avg_prefix_length. map that to $/k tokens and you get the curves.
03:34 Maya: for concreteness, with your sample traffic and a 35% cache hit-rate we estimate a 28% reduction in $/k tokens when using adaptive batching + prefix cache vs no cache + default small batch.
03:46 Liam: 28% is compelling. what's the impact on tail latency at that point?
03:51 Carlos: in our test, median latency remained similar, p95 moved by +10-15ms depending on model size; larger models show slightly more variance. we can tune batch windows to meet your p95 SLO.
04:06 Sophie: what about cold start for cache -- on first use hit-rate is zero, so initial cost spikes?
04:10 Arjun: yep that's why we recommend a warm-up phase as part of the pilot -- pre-populate KV with high-frequency prefixes from a daily job. that reduces the cold period dramatically.
04:18 Sophie: and is the warm-up safe from data leakage? some prefixes include PII.
04:22 Carlos: good call. we recommend tokenization-level hashing for keys and strict ACLs. also optional client-side token filtering so PII never reaches persistent cache. and for regulated customers you can limit cache to non-PII prompts only.
04:38 Rita: ok that's useful. another question: how does fallback work if the dedicated pool is congested? do requests go to hosted models?
04:46 Maya: yes -- smart routing has policies: fail open to hosted model variant (with tenant isolation) or queue with backpressure. default enterprise policy is failover to compatible model family in another region or lower tier. it's configurable per-route.
05:01 Liam: need to confirm whether any data hits public hosted environment during failover -- we have policy constraints.
05:06 Maya: noted, we'll include that in the security docs -- we support private-only fallback (reject) for strict profiles.
05:12 Sophie: can you show the console estimate for a sample week of traffic?
05:16 Carlos: yep -- loading your supplied profile (we used the sample you sent), here's the cost breakdown: compute, storage (KV), egress, infra overhead. compute dominates. this chart maps hit-rate along the x-axis and $/k tokens on y; you can see steep savings up to 40% hit-rate, then taper.
05:42 Carlos: one more nuance -- KV cache increases memory footprint on the serving nodes; if hit-rate grows we recommend using a separate cache tier (Redis or in-process depending on latency). we show recommended sizing in the console -- for your QPS it suggests a 2 node cache cluster on dedicated.
06:02 Sophie: for the pilot can we start with hosted + dedicated burst? we want to validate cost first.
06:08 Maya: yes common pattern: start hosted to instrument, then spin a small dedicated pool for steady traffic with autoscaling and burst to hosted. that gives a safety net.
06:17 Liam: performance testing -- what does Redwood need from us?
06:20 Carlos: we need sample prompt set, token distributions, expected qps, and a small subset for latency-sensitive routes. we'll run both baseline and with caching enabled.
06:30 Sophie: we'll share that after the call.
06:32 Maya: security questions?
06:34 Rita: you mentioned KMS/HSM -- do you support customer-managed keys in hosted?
06:38 Carlos: yes, BYOK is available for Private and Dedicated; for Hosted we support a managed KMS with customer key option in enterprise plans. we'll send KMS integration docs.
06:48 Sophie: also SOC 2 report?
06:50 Maya: we'll attach SOC 2 and our network diagram.
06:53 Liam: rough timeline -- if we get the benchmark done next week, we could be pilot-ready in 2-3 weeks?
06:59 Maya: that's reasonable. we'll follow up with scheduling.
07:02 Arjun: small product note -- Optimize can auto-suggest TTLs per-prompt family based on observed reuse, we'll include suggested configs in the workbook.
07:12 Sophie: any gotchas with multi-tenant cost attribution? we need per-route cost breakdowns.
07:18 Carlos: console provides per-route token breakdown and per-token cost mapping; we also stream detailed traces to your observability endpoint if you want.
07:27 Maya: ok let's recap next steps: we'll send cost workbook, SOC2/KMS docs, benchmark plan; Atlas to share traffic profile and sample prompts; schedule pilot kickoff week of April 6.
07:40 Rita: sounds good. thanks everyone, that was helpful.
07:44 Maya: thanks all -- we'll follow up via email with links.

End of transcript.
